title: Marine Aide (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (3381), DC I&L
raw_text:
2.     MOS 3372, Marine Aide (MGySgt to Cpl) NMOS (3381), DC I&L

    a. Summary. Marine Aides are authorized for the purpose of relieving
general and flag officers of those minor tasks and details that if performed
by the officer, would be at the expense of the officer's primary military and
official duties. The duties of these enlisted personnel shall be concerned
with tasks relating to the military and official responsibilities of
officers, to include assisting general and flag officers in discharging their
official DoD social responsibilities in their assigned positions. The
propriety of such duties is governed by the official purpose that they serve
rather than the nature of the duties. Marine Aides may be tasked to assist
with the care, cleanliness and order of assigned quarters, uniforms and
military personal equipment, perform as point of contact in the officer's
quarters, assist in planning, preparing, and conducting official social
functions, assist in purchasing, preparing, and serving food and beverages in
the officer's assigned quarters, and accomplish tasks which aid the officer
in performing his military and official responsibilities, including providing
security for the quarters and providing administrative assistance.

       b.    Prerequisites

             (1) Must be a volunteer.

             (2) Must be a minimum of 21 years of age.



                                         3-272                      Enclosure (1)
 3127                                                                     NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) Must meet all regular retention standards.

            (4) Must epitomize the “Whole Marine Concept”.

            (5) Preferred primary MOS 3381 for target assignment.

            (6) Security requirement:     must be eligible for a secret clearance.

        (7) Screening: Prior to formal acceptance into the Marine Corps
Enlisted Aide Program (MCEAP), Marines who possess the primary MOS 3381 may
be offered the opportunity to voluntarily work with Marines already assigned
to the MCEAP. This recruitment opportunity is a direct benefit to the
individual Marine providing firsthand exposure to the MCEAP, which will
assist the Marine with his/her decision to apply for the MCEAP. This
recruitment effort also benefits the MCEAP by increasing the number of
Marines available to make the MCEAP a success on a daily basis while at the
same time creating a more knowledgeable 3381 workforce. The Senior Marine
Corps Enlisted Aide in the command will administer this recruitment effort
ensuring that all 3881 Marines are provided an equal opportunity to gain this
experience.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Food Service NCO Course (A1433N1) at the corporal
level and the Food Service SNCO Course (A14DA21) at the staff sergeant level.
Prior to assignment to general officer quarters must attend the Advanced
Culinary and Skills Training Course (A14FAR3), Enlisted Aide Training Course
(A14F323), and Bartending School. The Bartending School is funded by the
Marine Corps Enlisted Aide Program currently assigned under Marine Barracks
Washington, DC.

        (2) The following course of instruction is desirable as a skill
progression course for MOS 3372: Professional Cook Skills Culinary Institute
of America, Hyde Park, NY and Napa Valley, CA. This course is funded by the
Marine Corps Enlisted Aide Program currently assigned under Marine Barracks
Washington, DC.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference (x), Food Service Training and Readiness Manual.

       e.   Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code

            (1) Executive Secretaries and Administrative Assistants 43-6011.

            (2) Purchasing Agent 162.157-038.

       f.   Related Military Skill.     Food Service Specialist, 3381.
common_text: The Marine Corps Food Service Occupational Field (OccFld) includes the acquisition of food, services, supplies, and equipment, menu and recipe planning, meal preparation and serving, food safety and sanitation, operation and management of facilities and personnel, training, budget reporting and fiscal accounting, accountability of subsistence and food supplies, accountability of meals and consumption reporting, messing services and functions for garrison and field food service operations. Qualifications required include basic math, reading administrative, managerial skills, the ability to follow recipes, and the ability to work closely with others. Duties include those incidental to the preparation and production of meal service. Food service personnel will be required to learn garrison and field food preparation and serving procedures, recipe conversions, the preparation and use of food service administrative forms, internal procedures to ensure food safety and quality assurance procedures for food processing, basic knowledge about mess hall operations, basic nutrition and human performance optimization methods, methods of cooking food in accordance with recipe instructions, methods of preparing desserts and beverages by using recipes/ formulas, and the proper storage and safekeeping of Class I subsistence supplies. Formal schooling is provided to Marines entering the food service 33XX OccFld. Types of entry-level jobs available include work as a Food Service Specialist. The opportunity to participate in a formal apprenticeship program leading to receipt of a Department of Labor Certificate of Apprenticeship Completion may be available within OccFld 33XX. Specific information concerning this program can be obtained from local education offices. Billets available in the OccFld range from duty within the operating forces and supporting establishment. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 3300, Basic Food Service Marine. They will participate in routine food service functions while training for a designated MOS within the OccFld.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
